messages:
Mira: quick sync — RFC follow-up on ephemeral vs long-lived keys for services. ops flagged issuance load and telemetry gaps. want tradeoffs + routing/issuer ideas. cc @Dan @Shankar
Dan: we ran ephemerals for a worker fleet last quarter; token churn spiked auth-server CPU and auth latency during bursts :/
Shankar: tradeoff summary: ephemerals = lower blast radius but need a robust refresh/mint path. options: central minting service, regional brokers, or signed short-lived JWTs minted locally from HSM. each has perf/complexity/security tradeoffs.
devops-bot: AUTH-METRICS: current auth-server peak QPS=1200, issuance p95 latency=49ms, 95% requests <50ms.
Sam: regional broker + caching of signed proofs seems promising — reduces cross-region hops and lowers auth-server QPS, but increases deployment surface and sync complexity.
Elaine: observability note — long-lived keys give stable identity mapping; ephemerals need propagated parent_id / issuer_id so logs/traces can rehydrate the caller quickly. otherwise we lose attribution.
Dan: what about hybrid: long-lived service key used only to mint ephemerals; runtime calls use ephemerals. that limits exposure of long-lived to bootstrap only.
Mira: agree. API sketch: service authenticates with long-lived to /mint and receives scoped ephemeral token. propose minimal shape:
```
POST /mint
Auth: Bearer svc-key-xxxx
Body: {"scope": "ingest:write", "ttl": 600}
Response: {"token": "ey...", "expires_at": "2026-03-28T12:34:56Z"}
```
Shankar: security concern: if svc-key is compromised attacker can mass-mint. mitigations: strict rate-limiting, issuer binding (aud claim), and mint request authz checks. also consider minting ACLs per svc-key.
Dan: revocation model: short TTL (<=15m) + active revocation cache on brokers. compromise -> invalidate in cache and propagate. chasing revocation for many tokens is hard, so favor short ttl + anomaly detection.
Elaine: RBAC mapping: ephemeral token should carry actor_id and explicit granted_roles claim to avoid repeated introspection lookups. include origin_service and parent_key_id.
Mira: ops asks for metrics to track: mint QPS, mint failure rate, avg latency, active tokens by service, revocation events. who can prototype?
Sam: :thumbsup: I can prototype a local broker + redis-backed revocation cache + simple mint API. ETA 1 week.
devops-bot: Created ticket INF-2456: "ephemeral-mint-broker-poc" assigned to Sam, due 2026-04-01.
Mira: awesome — we'll capture API contract as RFC addendum and define rollout plan (canary region -> global). will follow up in this thread with design doc link. closing sync for now, post updates here.
